cases.description: Plain LF-terminated ASCII list passes through unchanged.
CRLF line endings lose the CR (a control) and keep the LF.
Valid UTF-8 with CRLF is never double-encoded and loses only the CR (PfbFeedNormalizeTest: valid UTF-8 reaches sed without the converter).
A lone CR inside a line is stripped as a control, welding the two halves (PfbFeedNormalizeTest).
Classic-Mac CR-only line endings: no LF ever splits a line, so the CRs vanish and one welded line remains, then gets its final LF.
Trailing runs of spaces and tabs are removed per line, in any mix.
Interior tabs survive (hosts/TSV data); the trailing tabs go (PfbFeedNormalizeTest).
Consecutive interior spaces are data and stay; only the trailing run goes.
Leading spaces and tabs are not trimmed (only the end of a line is).
A whitespace-only line becomes an empty line; line count is preserved.
NUL, BEL, ESC and DEL are non-printable and are stripped wherever they sit.
VT and FF are control characters: stripped inside a line.
Controls are stripped and a clean trailing space run is trimmed (PfbFeedNormalizeTest).
A run of consecutive controls is removed whole, at the start, middle and end of a line.
One sed g pass never rescans: the space before a stripped control is no longer trailing after the removal, and stays.
Same no-rescan effect for a tab: the tab is not matched by the control class and stays.
Spaces before a stripped control stay; the space run after it is the real trailing run and goes.
BEL then CR (CRLF file with a stray BEL) is one non-printable run: the space before it stays.
A control followed by spaces: the control goes and the spaces after it are the trailing run.
A one-line file without a final LF gets one (PfbFeedNormalizeTest, issue #1263).
Only the last line lacks its LF; the guarantee appends exactly one.
An empty file stays empty: no newline is invented.
A file of only LFs is unchanged.
A file with only trailing-type whitespace and no LF normalizes to empty, and stays empty (no newline appended).
A file of only controls normalizes to empty.
Blank trailing text after the last LF is trimmed to nothing; the file keeps its final LF.
A 100000-character line (trailing BEL and spaces) normalizes without truncation or splitting.
A 300-character hostname is data: untouched.
A 5000-character line of tab-separated cells keeps every interior tab; only the trailing run goes.

cases.description: Valid multibyte IDN text (Latin, CJK, Cyrillic) and punycode labels are printable data: untouched.
Emoji (astral code points and a skin-tone modifier) are printable: untouched.
U+0085 and U+009B are valid UTF-8 but C1 controls: stripped.
U+2028 and U+2029 are not printable: stripped inside a line.
A U+FFFD already in valid UTF-8 text is printable data and stays.
UTF-16LE ASCII text without a BOM is byte-wise valid UTF-8 (NUL is valid): it passes the gate and the sed pass strips the NULs. Not a rule-C row; the converter is never consulted.
UTF-8 BOM U+FEFF is non-printable on the appliance: stripped from the first line.
BOM U+FEFF and ZWJ U+200D are non-printable (Cf) on the appliance and are stripped (PfbFeedNormalizeTest).
A ZWJ emoji sequence loses its joiners (U+200D is non-printable on the appliance); the emoji stay.
NBSP U+00A0 is printable and [:space:] on the appliance: kept inside a line, trimmed at the end (PfbFeedNormalizeTest).
NBSP mixed into a trailing space run is trimmed with it; a NBSP-only line becomes empty.

Pins the raw-byte fallback, not last-known-good: a binary file (bytes 0x00..0xFF) is neither empty nor a previous result; controls are stripped, tab trimmed at the line end, and every invalid byte 0x80..0xFF passes through untouched. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).

Pins the raw-byte fallback, not last-known-good: invalid UTF-8 (a Latin-1 e-acute byte) with a BEL keeps the raw byte and loses the BEL (PfbFeedNormalizeTest). Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).
Latin-1 hosts with CRLF endings: raw bytes kept, CRs stripped (PfbFeedNormalizeTest body shape). Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).
Windows-1252 smart quotes (0x91..0x94) are invalid UTF-8 bytes: passed through, CRLF trimmed. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).
UTF-16LE text with a non-ASCII char and no BOM is not UTF-8: raw bytes, NULs stripped, the e-acute low byte passes through. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).
Spaces after an invalid byte are the trailing run and are trimmed. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).
An invalid byte is matched by neither class: spaces before it are not trailing and stay. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).
Invalid UTF-8 without a final LF: raw bytes kept and the LF guarantee still applies. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).

A multibyte sequence cut off at end of file (an 8-KiB sample cap or an aborted download) passes through as invalid bytes. Unprobed on FreeBSD sed. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).

CESU-style encoded surrogate ED A0 80 is invalid UTF-8: each byte passes through. FreeBSD libc rejecting surrogates is assumed, unprobed. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).
Overlong C0 AF is invalid UTF-8: both bytes pass through. Unprobed on FreeBSD sed. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).

F4 90 80 80 (above U+10FFFF) is invalid UTF-8 to Go and to FreeBSD libc (assumed); glibc iconv accepts it, but the gate never changes the outcome here. Unprobed on FreeBSD sed. Core follows the conversion-unavailable path (owner rule, #3906).

UTF-16LE with BOM and CRLF decodes to UTF-8 LF lines. Core decodes BOM-marked UTF-16 itself (owner rule, #3906); the old path decodes it through charset_normalizer and pfb_feed_normalize.py (utf_16, errors=replace).

UTF-16BE with BOM and CRLF decodes to UTF-8 LF lines. Core decodes BOM-marked UTF-16 itself (owner rule, #3906); the old path decodes it through charset_normalizer and pfb_feed_normalize.py (utf_16, errors=replace).

UTF-16LE with BOM, non-ASCII and an astral char (surrogate pair) decodes to the right UTF-8. Core decodes BOM-marked UTF-16 itself (owner rule, #3906); the old path decodes it through charset_normalizer and pfb_feed_normalize.py (utf_16, errors=replace).

UTF-16BE with BOM, non-ASCII and an astral char (surrogate pair) decodes to the right UTF-8. Core decodes BOM-marked UTF-16 itself (owner rule, #3906); the old path decodes it through charset_normalizer and pfb_feed_normalize.py (utf_16, errors=replace).

Decoded UTF-16 text then gets the same per-line trailing trim. Core decodes BOM-marked UTF-16 itself (owner rule, #3906); the old path decodes it through charset_normalizer and pfb_feed_normalize.py (utf_16, errors=replace).

A BOM-marked UTF-16LE file without a final newline gets one after decoding. Core decodes BOM-marked UTF-16 itself (owner rule, #3906); the old path decodes it through charset_normalizer and pfb_feed_normalize.py (utf_16, errors=replace).

A BOM and nothing else decodes to empty (no newline invented). Core decodes BOM-marked UTF-16 itself (owner rule, #3906); the old path decodes it through charset_normalizer and pfb_feed_normalize.py (utf_16, errors=replace).

A BE BOM and nothing else decodes to empty. Core decodes BOM-marked UTF-16 itself (owner rule, #3906); the old path decodes it through charset_normalizer and pfb_feed_normalize.py (utf_16, errors=replace).

UTF-32LE ASCII starts FF FE 00 00, a UTF-16LE BOM plus a NUL. The old path detects utf_32; Core decodes it as UTF-16LE and the NULs are stripped: both give the same text for ASCII (UTF-32 is not ported). Core decodes BOM-marked UTF-16 itself (owner rule, #3906); the old path decodes it through charset_normalizer and pfb_feed_normalize.py (utf_16, errors=replace).

UTF-16LE with BOM and one stray trailing byte: the byte becomes U+FFFD. Deviation (owner rule, #3906): Core decodes the BOM-marked UTF-16 like the utf_16 codec with errors=replace; the old path's charset_normalizer refuses malformed UTF-16 ("no encoding match") and normalizes the raw bytes (old_expect).

UTF-16BE with BOM and a lone high surrogate mid-stream: one U+FFFD, the text after it is kept. Deviation (owner rule, #3906): Core decodes the BOM-marked UTF-16 like the utf_16 codec with errors=replace; the old path's charset_normalizer refuses malformed UTF-16 ("no encoding match") and normalizes the raw bytes (old_expect).

UTF-16LE with BOM and a lone low surrogate mid-stream: one U+FFFD, the text after it is kept. Deviation (owner rule, #3906): Core decodes the BOM-marked UTF-16 like the utf_16 codec with errors=replace; the old path's charset_normalizer refuses malformed UTF-16 ("no encoding match") and normalizes the raw bytes (old_expect).

UTF-16LE with BOM ending in a lone high surrogate: one U+FFFD. Deviation (owner rule, #3906): Core decodes the BOM-marked UTF-16 like the utf_16 codec with errors=replace; the old path's charset_normalizer refuses malformed UTF-16 ("no encoding match") and normalizes the raw bytes (old_expect).

The PfbFeedNormalizeTest Latin-1 body (40 repeats) with a working charset_normalizer. Deviation (owner rule, #3906): Core does not port charset detection and follows the conversion-unavailable path, keeping the raw bytes (expect); the old path detects Latin-1 and converts to UTF-8 (old_expect).
